en: During a thunderstorm, crouch low with your feet together to minimize your risk of being struck by lightning.
Always wear shoes when playing in soil because hookworm larvae can penetrate bare skin and cause severe intestinal infections.
Stagnant water left after heavy rain breeds Aedes aegypti mosquitoes, which transmit the deadly dengue virus to humans.
During an earthquake, hide under a sturdy table and hold its legs to protect your head from falling debris.
The mineral fluorite is the primary source of fluoride, which dentists add to toothpaste to prevent tooth decay.
The Sun emits ultraviolet radiation that can damage your skin, so you must wear sunscreen when playing outside.
The Moon's gravity creates high tides that can cause dangerous rip currents, so always swim near a lifeguard.
During extreme heat waves, drink plenty of water to prevent heatstroke, a dangerous condition where your body overheats.
When a volcano like Mount Taal erupts, wear an N95 mask to prevent inhaling fine ash that damages your lungs.
If a typhoon brings a storm surge, evacuate to higher ground immediately because the rising seawater can drown you.
You can find true north at night by locating Polaris, the North Star, which stays fixed above the North Pole.
Boil floodwater for at least one minute before drinking it to kill cholera bacteria and prevent severe diarrhea.
